good:
Your eval is your product spec. If you can't write the eval, you don't know what you're building.

I said this at PyCon India in Bengaluru last week. Most teams ship LLM features with zero evals. Vibes-based QA works fine until about 1k users. Then it breaks.

We wrote 40 golden examples for our support bot. Escalations dropped 31%.

The tooling was not the hard part. Agreeing on what 'good' means was. That argument is the spec.

If you're starting, pull 10 real examples from your logs. Not synthetic ones.

Someone asked if you need a framework. No. A spreadsheet.
